record.original_question: Fix c > 0. Among graphs on n vertices with cn² edges in which every edge lies in at least one triangle, let f(n; c) be the largest integer such that some edge is contained in at least f(n; c) triangles. Estimate f(n; c) as sharply as possible from above and below.

evidence.quote: Let G(n; cn²) be a graph on n vertices and cn² edges. Assume that every edge of our graph is contained in at least one triangle. Denote by f(n; c) the largest integer for which at least one edge is contained in at least f(n; c) triangles. Estimate f(n; c) as well as possible both from above and below.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Fix a constant $c>0$. For every positive integer $n$, consider all simple graphs $G$ on $n$ vertices with at least $cn^2$ edges such that every edge of $G$ is contained in at least one triangle (i.e., for every edge $uv\in E(G)$ there exists a vertex $w$ with $uw, vw\in E(G)$). For such a graph $G$, let $t(G)$ denote the maximum, over all edges $e\in E(G)$, of the number of triangles of $G$ containing $e$. Define
$$f(n;c) = \min_{G} t(G),$$
where the minimum is taken over all graphs $G$ on $n$ vertices satisfying the conditions above. Determine the asymptotic behavior of $f(n;c)$ as $n\to\infty$, providing matching upper and lower bounds as sharp as possible.
artifact.category_tag: Extremal graph theory / triangles in graphs
artifact.status_search_result: Fox and Loh (2012) showed that for every fixed c < 1/4, f(n;c) = n^{O(1/loglog n)}, refuting Erdős's conjecture that f(n;c) > n^ε for some ε=ε(c)>0. For c > 1/4, Turán-type arguments give f(n;c) ≥ n/6. The precise asymptotic of f(n;c) for c < 1/4 — in particular whether the upper bound n^{O(1/loglog n)} is tight — remains open.

status_evidence.title: On a problem of Erdős and Rothschild on edges in triangles
status_evidence.snippet: For every fixed c < 1/4, h(n,c) = n^{O(1/loglogn)}. This gives a negative answer to the question of Erdős from 1987.
status_evidence.claim: Fox and Loh established that f(n;c) grows much more slowly than any polynomial in n for c < 1/4, refuting Erdős's conjecture but not fully pinning down the asymptotics.

status_evidence.title: On a problem of Erdős and Rothschild on edges in triangles | Combinatorica
status_evidence.snippet: Published 2012; addresses Erdős–Rothschild problem on the number of triangles forced through some edge.
status_evidence.claim: The problem has been partially resolved in the regime c < 1/4.
